utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I have endeavoured to notify legal officer but didn't realise she was not in this afternoon. It is with sadness and concern that I inform the Chamber that the witness after Witness B has taken ill and has been ordered to his accommodation by the UN physician who was called in this morning, or earlier this afternoon. We hope that it is a passing event but that he has been -- it has been indicated he has been advised not at this point to appear this afternoon because of his condition. I have provided to a member of Your Honour's staff a copy of the name of the physician who is, again, part of the system, and as we are updated on anything, we will inform the Chamber. Defence counsel has also been advised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that mean that it remains a possibility that the witness will be able to attend tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We are optimistic that is the case. The -- my understanding from my colleague was that he was advised not to do it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, it appears, then, that the hearing will not be able to continue today when the present witness has concluded evidence. We should have the witness in now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the president, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I remind you of the affirmation you made at the commencement of your evidence, which still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic. Can I indicate --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- because of circumstances, Mr. Petrovic, I'll be a little slow to start the clock running, so you can expect that you may have a little more time than we indicated yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. B. We shall continue our cross-examination now, the cross-examination that we began yesterday. First of all, please tell me, is it true that you arrived at Zarkovica on the 19th of November, 1991, you and your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. I think it was in mid-November, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If you're not sure about the exact date, then why in your statement dated the 15th of June, 2002, on page 5, did you state decidedly as follows: "We arrived at Zarkovica in the evening of the 19th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I ever actually said that. Whenever I gave a statement, I always spoke in terms of mid-November. That's what I remembered, that it was the 17th or possibly the 18th, because I remember that. The day we arrived at Zarkovica the reservists were listening to the radio, and the news was that Vukovar had fallen, so that's what I remember and why I remember it, but I can't give you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I want to say that, once again, I think this is a bit out of context because it's two paragraphs. In the first paragraph he says: "I'm not sure about the date, but I think it was the 18th or 19th of November." And in another paragraph he says: "We reached it on the same evening of the 19th of November," but he gives an equivocal statement on the date. It's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my learned friends, it is with a great deal of surprise that I must observe that my learned friend has quoted this sentence inaccurately and only by halves. The witness actually said on the 18th or the 19th of November they arrived at Ivanica. There is no dispute about the fact at least in terms of the witness's statement in relation to Zarkovica. If you could please look at page 5 of the Serbian text, dear friend, I'm not -- he says, "I'm not sure about the date," but this is being said in relation to Ivanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. I'm corrected. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. B, at any rate, you didn't say what is reflected in the statement, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I please be allowed to have a look?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On page 5 of the B/C/S text, can you please look at paragraph 3 from the bottom up. Page 5, paragraph 3, from the bottom up, the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. May I just have a minute, please. If you ask me, this has been entered incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let's move on. Was it on the same day that Vukovar fell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was that same day that Vukovar fell. The day we arrived at Zarkovica, they were talking about the fall of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If you could go down one paragraph and look at that. The second sentence: "I remember that Vukovar fell on that day."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We heard that over the radio. But as far as I know, on the radio they kept talking about the fall of Vukovar for at least a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. B, the noun you used here in the statement is day in the singular, on that day Vukovar fell. Let's move on, however. I think the statement speaks for itself. Is it true that the first time you saw Captain Kovacevic was then, on the 19th of November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think I had seen him before at Duzi when we were on leave, but I can't be sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe -- did counsel give the Court a copy of the statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There have been corrections made to the statement, and they were notified about corrections. So some of the dates are wrong. This witness corrected a week ago some of the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We don't appear to have any corrections in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... provided for is that a prior inconsistent statement, are they introducing the statement, is it to refresh the witness's recollection. I don't understand why the statement is being offered. I have no objection, but that with the corrections, with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're going to find out, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Weiner, I'm showing this statement to the witness because the witness has five different statements, and in each of them he says a different thing. I think that in itself justifies the showing of the statement and why I'm asking questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can show the statement to the witness to refresh his recollection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, if each counsel would address the Chamber and not each other, we will proceed with better decorum.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I apologise. If they want to show it to the witness to refresh his recollection, that's one thing. If they want to offer it, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. then there's a way to offer it. Right now are they using it to impeach him? Then it doesn't go to the Court until it's being used for impeachment value, in that situation. If it is going to go in, I think we have the right to at least include the corrections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are technically perfectly correct, Mr. Weiner. Does that mean that from now on that will be observed by the Prosecution as well as the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I raised the same issue in the Stringer matter on the first day of testimony when they -- they introduced the exhibit before -- they just gave it out to the Court prior to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe on one basis or another the statement will come to be admissible, and I'm prepared to act in faith at the moment that that will be the case. I'm sure Mr. Petrovic has heard what you had to say. Carry on, please, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. But this sort of intervention on the part of my learned friend and colleague cuts my time even shorter in a manner of speaking, and I'm not particularly well off in terms of time. Therefore, I think he, too, should limit his objections to what is absolutely essential. I think the way I have proceeded with this cross-examination has been perfectly clear and fair so far. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On page 6 of your statement, Mr. B, as opposed to what you told the Chamber awhile ago, we see the following in the third paragraph from the bottom up: "The first time I saw him, Captain Vladimir Kovacevic, was on the 19th of November." Is that wrong too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said awhile ago, I am sure that I saw him for the first time on that day when we arrived at Zarkovica. I did say, however, that I may have seen him at Duzi as well but I wasn't sure about it. I am, however, sure about this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, when you say the first time I saw Vladimir Kovacevic was on the 19th of November, you don't actually mean it, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure, again, that I saw him on the 18th or 19th, whatever the day was that we arrived in Zarkovica. I'm sure I saw him then, but I'm not sure that I had previously seen him at Duzi. I may have, but I can't be sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on, please. Further, Mr. B, is it true that you said to Mr. Weiner during the interview that you had with him that on the 5th of December nothing unusual happened at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your statement dated the 15th of June, 2002, you talked about that day, the 6th of December, and that there was only a minimum of firing from the town of Dubrovnik. Is that what you said in that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was speaking about that, I was speaking in relation to the general Dubrovnik area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind, then, as to tell us about this: You're sitting at Zarkovica. What can you tell about the general Dubrovnik area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until perhaps when I got back home from the army, I had never been able to distinguish between the Old Town and the remaining parts. All I knew about was Dubrovnik, and that is why I kept using the name Dubrovnik as I was giving my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So back when you were at Zarkovica, you were not able to distinguish between the Old Town and the New Town, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time I was able, but whenever I referred to it later on, I would just say Dubrovnik meaning the general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So when was it that you understood what the distinction was between the Old Town and the New Town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Zarkovica. But whenever I talked about it later, I always used the name Dubrovnik. I never introduced this distinction for the sake of conversation. Be it in private when I was talking to my family. I never drew the distinction between the Old Town and the New Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So when was it that you first began to distinguish between the Old Town and the New Town in Dubrovnik when talking to your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was it perhaps about the year 2000, give or take a year or two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to distinguish between the Old and New Town when the investigators came to see you, the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to distinguish between the Old Town and the other parts of Dubrovnik when the investigators came to see you and talk to you about these events, the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew what the whole thing was about when they came, but I kept referring to the whole thing as Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did they perhaps ask you something about the Old Town specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And when they asked you about the Old Town, what you were actually talking about was Dubrovnik as a whole, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depended on the way the question was posed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If you're not able to distinguish between the Old and New Town, whichever way the question is posed should be all the same to you, shouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several kinds of questions, you know. There are general questions being asked about the general Dubrovnik area, and there are specific questions being asked in relation to the Old Town as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Again I fail to understand you. You're not able to distinguish between the Old and New Town, so what does that have to do with it, what sort of question you're being asked, if it's just all the same to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't answer that question. I'm doing my best. I'm trying to answer, but I don't know how you expect me to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell my learned friend and colleague Weiner too that you were not able to distinguish between the Old and New Town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was able to, but whenever I was writing this, I always wrote Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Did you tell Mr. Weiner that you were not able to distinguish between the Old Town and the other parts of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please, Your Honour. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, when he wrote down on the last page of his own notes in relation to your conversation, I think, was wrong in that case, because the following is stated there: [In English] "The Old Town was a separate entity from Dubrovnik and referred to the whole area as Dubrovnik."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. If he's going to read it, why doesn't he read it in context? He's not reading that statement in context.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Weiner, could you please give me a hand? What else would you define as context in relation to this sentence? I would be very grateful for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I see the statement? I just sent the trial manager out to make copies for the Court, and I don't have mine in front of me but I know what I wrote, and I know the context of what it is. I can tell you what the context of what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll just move on in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have it. I have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're ready now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me the page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Last page, second last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The witness was called to give statements to the Croatian authorities in 1992 concerning the JNA attack on Dubrovnik from Zarkovica on 6 December 1991. He was also called to testify in a case against Zeljko Soldo for his participation in the attack on that date. In Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. his testimony, he indicated did he not seen Soldo on that date. He also mentions that he was not familiar with that area. For example, he did not know that the Old Town was a separate entity from Dubrovnik and referred to the whole area as Dubrovnik. In fact, he was not familiar with the other locations in the Old Town such as Bogisica park or certain other locations in the area of the municipality. This paragraph concerns his testimony in 1992, his statements in 1992. That's what the context was, not in 2004 in relation to his familiarity with the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll move on if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, I return to that question, the first question we asked, Mr. B. In your statement, you say as follows: "Firing...", that's the 15th of June 2002, the statement, you say: "Firing from the direction of the town of Dubrovnik was at a minimum." Would you please be so kind as to tell us specifically where this firing was coming from that was at a minimum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly which place it was in the surroundings of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there any firing coming from the town of Dubrovnik itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the following date when I spoke to the reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I believe I must interrupt you, Mr. B. My question was: Was there any firing from the town of Dubrovnik itself? It's a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I did not know exactly where the firing was coming from, from which part of the surroundings of Dubrovnik those three or four shells came.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What, then, do you define as the surroundings of Dubrovnik and what as the town itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say the town of Dubrovnik, I mean the entire town of Dubrovnik. When I say the surroundings, I mean the islet to the left or those settlements lower down from Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: For you the town of Dubrovnik is what you could see from Zarkovica, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of that populated area or settlement or area that you could see from Zarkovica, was there any firing coming from there on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure which area it was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any fire coming from the Croatian forces on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just heard those three or four shells which we felt on Zarkovica, that they fell in the area surrounding Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about Srdj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there any Croatian fire aimed at Srdj, hitting Srdj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand this question. What does this mean, Croatians forces at Srdj? What?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were Croatian forces shooting at the area between Srdj and Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were Croatian forces shooting at the area between Srdj and Bosanka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were Croatian forces shooting at the area between Srdj and Strincjera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this Strincjera is exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were Croatian forces shooting at the fort of Srdj itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Old Town or what? I didn't understand this question at all, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you distinguish between the fort of Srdj and the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The -- Srdj is that turret up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean turret?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- on the right hand -- the one on the right-hand side where JNA units were attacking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were Croatian forces firing at that turret that you call Srdj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether -- whether they were, but JNA forces were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about these three or four shells around Zarkovica? Is that the only firing that came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know of these three or four shells near Zarkovica. I don't know about other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about that perhaps, Mr. B?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. B, can Srdj be seen from Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And on that day you didn't notice anything? You didn't notice any Croatian fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see anything. I only saw the Yugoslav forces withdrawing from Srdj. When they moved toward Srdj and when they were moving back from Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were there any armed Croatian soldiers in the town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I was not in Dubrovnik, and from Zarkovica I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there any resistance coming from the Croatian forces from the town of Dubrovnik aimed at the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that three or four shells fell there from the area surrounding Dubrovnik, but which place exactly I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were there any armed Croatian soldiers in the town of Dubrovnik and in the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were these shells perhaps fired by someone else? Perhaps they weren't fired by the Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, very close to the place where you were, there was a communications platoon, a signals platoon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was this signalsman at Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 6th of December the signalsman on duty was Captain Nesic's signalsman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this signalsman of Captain Nesic had a military telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this signalsman, during the course of that day, the 6th of December, maintained communication with other JNA units in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who he maintained communication with. I know that a few times he ran towards Kovacevic with that device, and who they were in communication with is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Kovacevic use that telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him a few times during the course of that day using that telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him about twice, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see a cable that went from that place where Captain Nesic's headquarters were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which area do you mean? The cable went in which direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you saw a cable.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw -- I remember a cable that went from that communications centre towards Brgat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask that the witness please be shown the following statement. Your Honours, unfortunately, this witness statement was not translated into English because it was disclosed by the Prosecution to the Defence without an English translation only a few days ago, that is to say, the statement is dated the 21st of April, 1992, and we're going to do our best to have it translated. Also, could the statement dated the 1st of December, 1992, be distributed as well so that we don't waste too much time. Fortunately, that statement does have an English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Once again, we'd object to any statements until there's a legal basis for introducing them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We did not resolve the position of the statement that you first put to the witness, that of the 13th, the 15th of June, 2002, Mr. Petrovic. Are you proposing to tender that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order to save time, I wanted to deal with all three statements at the same time in order to save time. If you allow me to do so, that's what I'm going to do. If not, then I will ask to tender the first statement and then I'll repeat that for the next statements, too, and I can give the reasons why I'm asking for that, if that is absolutely indispensable and if my colleague Mr. Weiner objects to having it tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it your basis of tendering that you suggest that each of these are inconsistent in some respect with the evidence given by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all three statements are totally inconsistent with what the witness said during the examination-in-chief, and basically the objective, why I'm asking for this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying they're inconsistent in all respects or that there is at least one matter in which there is inconsistency?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is an enormous number of inconsistencies. However, guided by the restrictions imposed on the Defence in terms of cross-examination, I cannot indicate all of them, but there is a great many of them. I can start from the very beginning and point out each and every discrepancy, but that would not be in line with your decision that was rendered to us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, do you persist with your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If the Court is interested in accepting those, and I don't agree that it's fully inconsistent, there are some inconsistencies, I'd ask we have the corrections and the supplement also introduced. Generally in this Tribunal prior inconsistent statements aren't, but I would ask that the supplement also be provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that would be the better course to take in the circumstances. We propose to receive these statements, Mr. Petrovic, when you come to tender them, but we would also want to see the corrections that were made available before the evidence was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- Your Honour, thank you for the first part of your conclusion. But as for the second part, I have to note that there are no statements or corrections made by the witness himself. There is only the notes made by Mr. Weiner, but that is not the witness's statement. We saw one example yesterday. The witness did not mention at all the things that are contained in Mr. Weiner's proofing report that was not signed. So I believe that legally the two cannot be treated the same way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are not following strict and normal procedure as a convenience to you, Mr. Petrovic, and because of time. If you are putting these to the Chamber with a view to inviting us to form the view that the witness is unreliable because of differences in former statements, without taking the witness to each of the material differences, not all the minor discrepancies but the things that matter, then it is only fair both to the Chamber and to the witness that we are informed of changes of which you were notified before he gave his evidence. So the position is if you are tendering these three statements, we wish to receive, whether from you or from the Prosecution, those changes that were notified, accepting that you were notified merely in the form of notes made by Mr. Weiner rather than in the form of a further formal statement. Now, do you have those corrections available or shall we get them in due course from Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe we will get them from my colleague Mr. Weiner. Could I please ask to have this document distributed, too, please. Thank you, Your Honour. Could the next statement be distributed as well, please. That's the one that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. B, these two statements that are in front of you, are they the statements that you made, one to the police in Bjelovar on the 21st of April, 1992, and the second one to the district court in Bjelovar on the 1st of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my signature is there, then probably they are my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to look at both statements.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They're all signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. B, that in your statement dated the 21st of April, 1992, you do not mention anywhere any operations in November 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your statement of the 21st of April, 1992, you do not mention any operations anywhere, any operations that took place in November 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: November. Is that the 11th month in the year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I see, this is not written properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That will do. Thank you. Is it correct that in your statement dated the 21st of April, 1992, you do not mention the attack of the 6th of December anywhere? Just briefly, please, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but could you just repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you have problems hearing me, understanding me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. You ask me and then I start reading, and then I forget what you asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your statement dated the 21st of April, 1992, you do not mention the attack of the 6th of December, 1991, anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot read anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you do not mention it anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably not. I gave answers in respect of what they asked me in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your statement dated the 21st of April and the 1st of December, 1992, you do not mention any line-up of your unit by Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because nobody asked me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your statement dated the 1st of December, 1992, you do not mention any operations in the month of November 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because nobody asked me about that. They asked me about the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your statements of the 21st of April and the 1st of December, 1992, you do not mention any kind of competition or game played by the reservists in Zarkovica in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I perhaps do not need to read it again. I will just give you the same answer yet again. If nobody asks me about it, then I do not mention it. There were different questions. Every time they put different questions to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Oh, so somebody put questions to you whether there were any games played at Zarkovica? Later somebody asked you about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'll give you an example.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just give me a yes or no answer. Did anybody ask you later on whether there were any games played at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody put that kind of question to me, whether there were any games at Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that in your statements of the 21st of April and the 1st of December, 1992, you do not mention anywhere that the Old Town was targeted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. Again, I must point out that I was talking about Dubrovnik at -- in a very general way, not the Old Town specifically. But that's what I had in mind, just the word I was using was Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on two different occasions yesterday, on pages 17 and 33 of the transcript, you told us that the first time you heard about the Old Town was when Captain Delic told you when he came to see you? You said, "I was angry. That was the first time I heard about the Old Town."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, heard but not seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why, then, in your statement dated the 15th of June to the OTP investigators, on page 5 of your statement, you said that you had heard from Vukalovic that Delic had been saying something to the soldiers about the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which page was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Third passage. The page is 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead why you told us two different things.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from both Vukalovic and Delic I hear the same thing. From Vukalovic I heard it at Ivanica and from Delic at Trebinje. It's just that I can't remember specifically which was the first occasion. I chanced on -- across Captain Delic in Trebinje just out in the street and he had been wounded in his leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That is not an inconsistent statement. If you look in the initially translation there is no inconsistency. There may be in the B/C/S version, which counsel is reading, but there is no inconsistency in the English statement. There are two clauses in that statement there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: With an "and" in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The text speaks for itself. Therefore, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, these police inspectors, the police inspectors who questioned you and the investigating judge who questioned you on the 21st of April and the 1st of December, 1992, were they able to distinguish between the Old Town and the rest of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object. He can't answer for the police inspectors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's sound enough, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it your submission, Mr. B, that neither the investigating judge nor the police officer asked you about the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In none of these three statements do you ever refer to a man named Vucurevic. How come you suddenly remember that man now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean how he occurred to me? Well, there was a question -- just a minute, please. I was watching a recording, and I saw Vucurevic in that recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: It said Vucurevic. His name was on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. On the 6th of December, in the morning, do you know --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 6th of December, 1991. What was happening at JNA positions at Bosanka, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As far as I knew, the infantry was stationed there, but I know nothing special about that because I'd never been to Bosanka myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was perhaps happening at JNA positions at Strincjera that same morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true what you told us yesterday on page 29 of yesterday's transcript? You said that you left the room in which you were staying two or three times, five or ten minutes each.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was two or three times. I stayed outside five or ten minutes each time. I went to the position itself to see the operator, because I was transporting the rockets, the missiles. I spent the remaining part of the time taking the rockets from one place to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That morning on that day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've had double the time we had in mind, Mr. Petrovic. Could I say that you should finish in the next five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it your submission that from the command of the Trebinje Brigade with which you did your military service until 1992 and which was active in the Dubrovnik operation -- zone of operations, the district which informs the recruitment office at Krizevci as to when you were discharged from the JNA, what your reward days were and which unit you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what they told me. I can't say that it's true or that it's not true. I can only go as far as to say what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on page 8 of your statement dated the 15th of June, 1992, you said as follows: "I'm sure that not a single soldier from my artillery battalion was promoted or rewarded in any way." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where exactly is that stated? Which paragraph is that? Will you tell me, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It's on page 8 of your statement dated the 15th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. However, reward time off was given to soldiers years after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: After the war; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I said after the war, I meant after the 6th of December. Because after the 6th of December, there was no --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Witness interrupted by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Kovacevic talk to the Maljutka operators on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you heard nothing of what he told them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard when he ordered them to shoot. What they talked about themselves, it was something that I was not able to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I now see myself compelled to bring my cross-examination to an end, although I do have some questions left. In addition to moving these statements into evidence, I would also like to ask to move into evidence the following document which by your leave I shall now distribute, and the document is -- my apologies. I had a problem with my headset. This is the judgement of the district court in Dubrovnik in relation to what I talked about yesterday, and the judgement precisely reflects what I showed the witness, namely that his statement was read out before the Court, that he was not there himself. I would like to move that statement into evidence because the best part of my cross-examination rests on that statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the speakers please kindly try not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, you were saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's something I wanted to say at the beginning but I was not allowed because the Defence kept saying something. There is -- there is an answer I would like to provide in relation to the Dubrovnik trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first time I was summoned to testify in Dubrovnik in the Zeljko Soldo trial, I can't remember which date that was, but I failed to respond to that summons. I had my own reasons. But the second time I was summoned, I responded, and that was about two weeks later. Zeljko Soldo was sentenced to 15 years in prison at that trial. That's what I heard later. However, a year or two later, I was summoned again to testify in a retrial of Zeljko Soldo. However, again I failed to respond to the first summons because a member of my family had just died. Of the course the second time around I responded to the summons. I was willing to respond to the summons but I was never summoned again, nor did I receive any further information. That's the clarification that I wish to provide in relation to this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, regardless of what the witness has just stated, may we have this document distributed, please, and may it be moved into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we have a moment? There's a lot of facts concerning the whole operation there, so I want to consult with counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that is happening, we'll deal with the statements. They will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I have the break to look at that; it's a 21-page document. I have a draft English translation of it. I'd like to look at it at the break and then answer when we return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're contemplating we will need to adjourn during your re-examination, are you, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I can go right ahead and re-examine. It won't be a long re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's what we anticipated. I suggest that consideration be given to the matter as you're re-examining by those about you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We can try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: See how it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I don't know if we have an English translation of the judgement -- of the verdict, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you have an English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a minute. Is there an English translation there in that large document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could the usher give one to Mr. Weiner. While that is happening, if the court officer would receive the three statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And we'd like to file the supplement. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first document, which is ERN number 00229067, will be marked as Defence Exhibit D67. The next document which bears the number, at the bottom, 00229046 will be marked as D68. The last document which is the witness information is marked D69. Under seal? Under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All three will be under seal. And now the corrections in the form they were notified.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The corrections -- the corrections will be marked D70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is correct they be given a Defence number in view of the condition upon which we've received the three preceding documents, and this, too, will be under seal. I think now we're ready for you, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may make a remark. The verdict that I would like to have moved into evidence was obtained from the OTP. The translation was also made by the OTP. In that translation, there are certain insufficiencies about which we will be informing you in writing. There are whole passages that are missing in that translation, but in order to avoid taking up any more of your time, we shall file a written motion about that. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just for -- just to add to that, Your Honour, if we do agree, I think we should put in the B/C/S version and have an official English translation done, because I tried to work with the draft translation today, and I agree it was filled with incorrect statements. So -- but we'll get back to you soon on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be convenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Witness B -- Witness B, you were asked a few minutes ago the following question about did you state the following: "I don't think any of the soldiers was rewarded or decorated as a result of the Dubrovnik campaign. I, however, cannot say anything about the senior officers. I am certain that no soldier from my division was promoted or rewarded." The remainder of the sentence from your statement in the year 2002 states: "However, reward time off was given to soldiers after the war. Some got 30 days off; others got 15 to 20 days off. I was not given any time off initially, but when I complained, I was given five reward days." Do you still agree with that statement that you previously made, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, is that why you were allowed to leave the military on January 23rd as opposed -- 1992, as opposed to February 1st?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the reason that I got the days off.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were asked about your various statements that you gave. Let's begin with the one in April 1992. Did you tell the police about the JNA attack from Zarkovica in early December 1991? Did you make that statement on 21st of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat that? I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown D67, 68, and 69, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the April 21st statement, please. And on the first page of that, sir, or the first -- the second page, do you talk about the JNA firing from Zarkovica in early December 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what is written here, that there was firing from Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then you later state in that statement: "They did not have a concrete, specific objective for firing at Dubrovnik itself, but they fired at hotels and tenement houses as well as the Old Town walls." Do you agree with that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you go to the next statement, D68, the one dated December 1, 1992. If you look at the first, second, third, fourth, fifth -- the sixth paragraph, the last paragraph on the first page -- or page 2. It begins: "On December 6th." It says: "On December 6th, 1991, the 3rd Battalion launched an attack on Dubrovnik and the surrounding area. I know that the battalion commander Vladimir Kovacevic issued the order to attack my company." Do you agree with that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And now could you look at the last statement, your statement to the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you talk about the JNA attack launched on December 6, 1991, in that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: What page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's -- try page 6. The bottom of 6, into page 7.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you indicated on that date that Kovacevic ordered you to fall in, spoke to you, and then ordered the attack; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked also yesterday if you knew an officer named Zec. In your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2002, you said: "I saw -- I also saw a number of other high-ranking JNA officers whose names I don't know visiting Zarkovica on 6 December. But I think they were -- I think they came in the afternoon when the operation was almost over. I think I saw Milan Zec once or twice during the whole operation. I am not sure whether I saw him on 6 December or some other day. Some days ago, I saw him on the TV, and I thought that I had seen him on Zarkovica at least once, but I don't remember the date when I saw him during the Dubrovnik operation. I never saw Miodrag Jokic throughout the operation." Do you still agree with that statement that you made to the Office of the Prosecutor in 19 -- sorry, in 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you saw the officers from a distance. Were you and the other Croatian soldiers ever given any orders about how you should act in the presence of JNA officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Tell the Court what you were told.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever somebody with a higher rank came to Zarkovica, I and the other Croat were ordered to withdraw into our own rooms, into any dormitory. Not only when officers came but also when journalists came.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had you ever gotten close to Commander Kovacevic while you served on Zarkovica? When I say "close," distance-wise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three times approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever speak with Commander Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never spoke to him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you allowed to approach Commander Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to anything that we had, any complaint or whatever, it went through Vukalovic or Nesic. I never even tried to get to Kovacevic because I knew it was impossible, and I didn't dare to either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were questioned about your military booklet. Who offered -- I'm sorry. Who gave you that military booklet, the JNA or someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: The new one, you mean, or the old one?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your new military booklet, the one -- the copy of which was presented into evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got that at the place where I live and where such military documents are issued. That's the military office.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you attempt to get some information from Trebinje in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only at the military office where the -- my booklet was issued. I went there a few times to have corrections made.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you successful in 1992 or later receiving any information from Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was the military office successful in receiving information from Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they never asked for anything from Trebinje. They told me when I got out of the army that they got information from Trebinje and that was it. It's not that they would ask for anything or that I could ask for anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, Trebinje is located in which state, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in the years 1992 to 1995, was Bosnia-Herzegovina involved in a war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And during that period, were you ever able to receive any assistance from Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in early April, at the end of March and early April, you talked about the four mortar shells -- two to four mortar shells that were fired into the area of Zarkovica. You stated you did not see the exact location where the mortar rounds came from, nor did anyone mention a location. Do you agree with that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one mentioned exactly where the shells had come from. The reservists later talked about why they were shooting at the Old Town if not a single shell was fired from the Old Town at Zarkovica. But where these shells came from is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You also stated that you and some of the Maljutka operators and suppliers hid in the dorms for safety - that's after those shells came into the area - and that the fire from the Croatian side did not last very long and no more shells were fired into the area of Zarkovica. Do you agree with that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were asked today whether you knew where the Croatian troops were located in the Dubrovnik municipality. Were you ever briefed by any of the officers in relation to the locations of the Croatian troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one ever told me their exact position, where they were. I did not see anyone either. I did not see any Croatian soldiers. I didn't see any from Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Finally, sir, there was some differences in dates in the documents, in the statements that had been provided. When you went from your farm into the military and to Zarkovica, did you maintain a diary? Did you keep a diary with you as to the daily events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Even if I had kept one, I would not have been able to keep it, like I haven't been able to keep any of the pictures that we had taken at Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just ask that the verdict be admitted into evidence and assigned a number as a Defence exhibit, if you so permit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Weiner, have you been able to cope with that difficult task?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. We have no objection. However, the translation is very poor. It should go to CLSS for a proper translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that would be a very good idea. We will receive the document now as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be D71.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that needs to be under seal as well, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because we have taken an unusual course with exhibits today, I think it useful to the record to record what we have done and why. We have received into evidence some previous statements of the witness. They are received at the instance of the Defence because it is their contention that those statements will reveal such inconsistencies that we should not accept the credit of the witness. Normally under the procedures of the Tribunal specific passages from previous statements would be put to the witness. Otherwise, the statements themselves would not be admitted. We had put Defence counsel under tight time constraints in cross-examination, and there were three statements, at least one of which was quite lengthy. We therefore followed the unusual course of receiving those statements. We received them solely for the purpose of assessing whether or not we should rely on the credibility of the witness in respect of the actual evidence given by the witness. The three statements and the correction in respect of them are not in themselves evidence of the actual facts of this case, except to the extent that any particular passages have been specifically put to the witness and accepted or rejected by that witness. I felt it important that that be made clear so that it is not suggested later to us or elsewhere that the whole contents of the statements are admitted as evidence of the actual facts of the case. Now, there is an uncertainty as to whether the witness who was to follow this witness will be available tomorrow. We have met this situation before. We will adjourn now in the expectation that the witness is well enough to give evidence tomorrow, and in that event, we will resume at the normal time tomorrow afternoon to hear that evidence. Should it be the case that the witness's ill health continues and there is no other witness available, if that could be communicated by the Prosecution to Ms. Musser, then in that event it will be possible for us not to sit tomorrow. Of course, that would need to be done in time to make arrangements to avoid the need for the accused to be brought into the Court tomorrow. And if that should occur, we will, of course, then resume again in the ordinary time at the next sitting day, which would be Friday. So we adjourn now in the expectation that we will be able to continue tomorrow, but that is subject to contingency. May I thank you for your attendance, Witness, and for the assistance that you have given. Once we have adjourned, you will be free to leave and to return to your home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of April, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.52 p.m.,
